How To Apply
Applying to Texas Tech
A Texas Tech University graduate degree opens doors, and applying is your first step. As a Red Raider, you’ll have the support behind you every step of the way.
Grad Application
Deadlines & Requirements
We strongly recommend that all students apply by our priority deadlines. While programs will continue to accept and review applications after these dates, admissions decisions and funding considerations are made on a first-come first-served basis.
Find Your Program Contact
Recommended Application Dates
Priority Application Dates
Spring: June 15
Summer & Fall: January 15
Application deadlines vary by program; contact your program of interest for specific dates. Because your admission application also serves as your application for departmental funding, such as assistantships and scholarships, we encourage you to apply by the priority deadline.
Fellowships
Apply by: February 3
Fellowships at Texas Tech
U.S. domestic students
Apply by: 3 months before classes start
Domestic Application Information
International students
Apply by: January 15/June 15, to allow time for immigration processing
International Application Information
Resources & Tips
Transcripts & Test Scores
Students must submit transcripts from all degree-awarding institutions. All documents received during the application process are considered unofficial, so please upload soft, PDF copies to your application portal. Official copies of these documents are required by the 12th class day of the term to which you are admitted.
Program Materials
Most Texas Tech graduate programs require supplemental materials for admission review. These materials may include (but are not limited to) items such as a statement of purpose, recommendations, writing samples, creative portfolio, etc. You can learn more about your intended program’s requirements at their webpage or by contacting the advisor.
Application Submission
Please ensure that you have uploaded everything you intend to include as part of your application prior to submitting. Applicants are unable to add or change any documents once the application has been submitted.
Generative AI Usage
As an emerging research institution, Texas Tech University values exploring new technologies, including generative AI tools like ChatGPT. However, we value the applicant’s unique voice in their personal statements, writing samples and other application materials. Should you use generative AI, it is important that the use only complements your original ideas and is not used to compose your work entirely. We hold prospective graduate students to the same academic integrity standards as our current students, and applicants are expected to abide by Texas Tech University’s policy on Academic Integrity.
